name: Na2SO4 thenardite, anhydrous sulfate
citation: F. C. Hawthorne and R. B. Ferguson. Anhydrous sulphates. I: Refinement of the crystal structure of celestite with an appendix on the structure of thenardite. The Canadian Mineralogist13 (1975),181–187.
recommendation: experimental source candidate; native FEFF and numerical validation pending
method: Experimental structure refinement of anhydrous thenardite in the appendix to the1975 study; COD/AMCSD preserve the thenardite coordinates. Publisher confirms article, year, volume, pages and experimental-structure classification.
notes: This article has no DOI in COD and no DOI exposed on the verified publisher record. doi is null; use the full article citation and primary_url, never invent a DOI.
Sulfur is global unique-site index2 (Na comes first), multiplicity8; all four O neighbors at1.479344A belong to the sulfate tetrahedron.
The file contains no hydrogen and is an ordered stoichiometric thenardite model. Na must remain in the full cluster/potential stoichiometry even though the selected shell is S–O.
Occupancy column is absent; full occupation is implicit in the ordered structure.
The article title begins with celestite; this COD entry is explicitly the appendix thenardite dataset, formulaNa2SO4, not SrSO4.
measurement_conditions_evidence: No measurement temperature/pressure in the downloaded CIF or verified publisher record; leave unknown. This is anhydrousNa2SO4, not mirabiliteNa2SO4·10H2O or high-temperatureNa2SO4 polymorphI.

occupancy.interpretation: Occupancy column absent; unit occupancy is parser interpretation, not an explicit refined occupancy.
